ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In $\triangle ABC$ shown in the figure, $AB=7$, $BC=8$, $CA=9$, and $\overline{AH}$ is an altitude. Points $D$ and $E$ lie on sides $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{AB}$, respectively, so that $\overline{BD}$ and $\overline{CE}$ are angle bisectors, intersecting $\overline{AH}$ at $Q$ and $P$, respectively. What is $PQ$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, and C is above; side AB is labeled 7, BC is labeled 8, and CA is labeled 9. H lies on side BC, and segment AH is drawn from A to BC and is an altitude. D is on AC, BD is drawn and intersects AH at Q; E is on AB, CE is drawn and intersects AH at P. Reasoning: By the analytic coordinate method, let B=(0,0), C=(8,0), making BC horizontal. Since AH is the altitude from A to BC, AH is perpendicular to BC, so set A=(x,y), and AH is a vertical line. From AB=7, AC=9, obtain x^2+y^2=49, (x-8)^2+y^2=81. Subtracting the two equations gives -16x+64=32, so x=2; hence y^2=49-4=45, take y=3√5, therefore A=(2,3√5), and AH is the line x=2. For CE, because CE is the angle bisector of angle C, E is on AB and AE:EB=AC:CB=9:8, so E=(8A+9B)/17=(16/17,24√5/17). The line CE goes from C=(8,0) to E; let a parametric point be C+t(E-C). Its x-coordinate is 8-120t/17; setting x=2 gives t=17/20, hence the y-coordinate of P is (17/20)(24√5/17)=6√5/5. For BD, because BD is the angle bisector of angle B, D is on AC and AD:DC=AB:BC=7:8, so D=(8A+7C)/15=(24/5,8√5/5). The line BD goes from B=(0,0) to D; let a parametric point be sD. Its x-coordinate is 24s/5; setting x=2 gives s=5/12, hence the y-coordinate of Q is (5/12)(8√5/5)=2√5/3. P and Q are both on the vertical line AH, so PQ equals the difference of the y-coordinates: PQ=6√5/5-2√5/3=(18-10)√5/15=8√5/15.

Put B=(0,0), C=(8,0), so BC is horizontal and AH is vertical. From AB=7 and AC=9, solve A=(2,3√5), hence AH is the line x=2. Use the angle bisector theorem: for CE, E lies on AB with AE:EB=AC:CB=9:8, so compute E as the weighted point on AB; intersect line CE with x=2 to get P. method.method_draft: Use a synthetic length-ratio approach with Menelaus. From the image, read that H lies on BC and AH is the altitude, with P and Q on AH. First compute the altitude geometry from the side lengths: Heron's formula gives area [ABC]=12√5, so AH=2[ABC]/BC=3√5. Also AB^2=AH^2+BH^2 gives BH=2 and hence CH=6. For Q, apply the angle bisector theorem to BD: AD:DC=AB:BC=7:8. In triangle ACH, the transversal B-D-Q crosses AC at D, AH at Q, and the extension of CH at B; Menelaus gives QH:QA=2:7, so QH=(2/9)AH=2√5/3. For P, apply the angle bisector theorem to CE: AE:EB=AC:CB=9:8. In triangle ABH, the transversal C-E-P crosses AB at E, AH at P, and the extension of BH at C; Menelaus gives PH:PA=2:3, so PH=(2/5)AH=6√5/5. Since P and Q both lie on AH, subtract: PQ=PH-QH=6√5/5-2√5/3=8√5/15.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中是三角形 ABC，A 在左下，B 在右下，C 在上方；H 位于边 BC 上，并画出了 AH。点 D 在边 AC 上，点 E 在边 AB 上；线段 BD 与 AH 相交于 Q，线段 CE 与 AH 相交于 P。图中标注了 AC=9，BC=8，AB=7。再推理：由 Heron 公式，半周长 s=(7+8+9)/2=12，面积 [ABC]=sqrt(12·5·4·3)=12sqrt(5)。因为 AH 是到 BC 的高，所以 AH=2[ABC]/BC=24sqrt(5)/8=3sqrt(5)。在直角三角形 ABH 中，AB^2=AH^2+BH^2，所以 7^2=(3sqrt(5))^2+BH^2，BH^2=49-45=4，BH=2。于是 CH=BC-BH=8-2=6。对于 Q，因为 BD 是角 B 的角平分线，由角平分线定理 AD:DC=AB:BC=7:8。在三角形 ACH 中，直线 B-D-Q 截 AC 于 D，截 AH 于 Q，且 B 在 CH 的延长线上。由 Menelaus 定理，(AD/DC)(CB/BH)(QH/QA)=1，即 (7/8)(8/2)(QH/QA)=1，所以 QH:QA=2:7。因此 QH=(2/(2+7))AH=(2/9)·3sqrt(5)=2sqrt(5)/3。对于 P，因为 CE 是角 C 的角平分线，由角平分线定理 AE:EB=AC:CB=9:8。在三角形 ABH 中，直线 C-E-P 截 AB 于 E，截 AH 于 P，且 C 在 BH 的延长线上。由 Menelaus 定理，(AE/EB)(BC/CH)(PH/PA)=1，即 (9/8)(8/6)(PH/PA)=1，所以 PH:PA=2:3。因此 PH=(2/(2+3))AH=(2/5)·3sqrt(5)=6sqrt(5)/5。P、Q 都在 AH 上，且 P 比 Q 离 H 更远，所以 PQ=PH-QH=6sqrt(5)/5-2sqrt(5)/3=(18sqrt(5)-10sqrt(5))/15=8sqrt(5)/15。

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 先描述图像：图中是三角形 ABC，A 在左下，B 在右下，C 在上方；H 位于边 BC 上，并画出了 AH。点 D 在边 AC 上，点 E 在边 AB 上；线段 BD 与 AH 相交于 Q，线段 CE 与 AH 相交于 P。图中标注了 AC=9，BC=8，AB=7。再推理：由 Heron 公式，半周长 s=(7+8+9)/2=12，面积 [ABC]=sqrt(12·5·4·3)=12sqrt(5)。因为 AH 是到 BC 的高，所以 AH=2[ABC]/BC=24sqrt(5)/8=3sqrt(5)。在直角三角形 ABH 中，AB^2=AH^2+BH^2，所以 7^2=(3sqrt(5))^2+BH^2，BH^2=49-45=4，BH=2。于是 CH=BC-BH=8-2=6。对于 Q，因为 BD 是角 B 的角平分线，由角平分线定理 AD:DC=AB:BC=7:8。在三角形 ACH 中，直线 B-D-Q 截 AC 于 D，截 AH 于 Q，且 B 在 CH 的延长线上。由 Menelaus 定理，(AD/DC)(CB/BH)(QH/QA)=1，即 (7/8)(8/2)(QH/QA)=1，所以 QH:QA=2:7。因此 QH=(2/(2+7))AH=(2/9)·3sqrt(5)=2sqrt(5)/3。对于 P，因为 CE 是角 C 的角平分线，由角平分线定理 AE:EB=AC:CB=9:8。在三角形 ABH 中，直线 C-E-P 截 AB 于 E，截 AH 于 P，且 C 在 BH 的延长线上。由 Menelaus 定理，(AE/EB)(BC/CH)(PH/PA)=1，即 (9/8)(8/6)(PH/PA)=1，所以 PH:PA=2:3。因此 PH=(2/(2+3))AH=(2/5)·3sqrt(5)=6sqrt(5)/5。P、Q 都在 AH 上，且 P 比 Q 离 H 更远，所以 PQ=PH-QH=6sqrt(5)/5-2sqrt(5)/3=(18sqrt(5)-10sqrt(5))/15=8sqrt(5)/15。

raw_record.original_question: In $\triangle ABC$ shown in the figure, $AB=7$, $BC=8$, $CA=9$, and $\overline{AH}$ is an altitude. Points $D$ and $E$ lie on sides $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{AB}$, respectively, so that $\overline{BD}$ and $\overline{CE}$ are angle bisectors, intersecting $\overline{AH}$ at $Q$ and $P$, respectively. What is $PQ$?
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, and C is above; side AB is labeled 7, BC is labeled 8, and CA is labeled 9. H lies on side BC, and segment AH is drawn from A to BC and is an altitude. D is on AC, BD is drawn and intersects AH at Q; E is on AB, CE is drawn and intersects AH at P. Reasoning: By the analytic coordinate method, let B=(0,0), C=(8,0), making BC horizontal. Since AH is the altitude from A to BC, AH is perpendicular to BC, so set A=(x,y), and AH is a vertical line. From AB=7, AC=9, obtain x^2+y^2=49, (x-8)^2+y^2=81. Subtracting the two equations gives -16x+64=32, so x=2; hence y^2=49-4=45, take y=3√5, therefore A=(2,3√5), and AH is the line x=2. For CE, because CE is the angle bisector of angle C, E is on AB and AE:EB=AC:CB=9:8, so E=(8A+9B)/17=(16/17,24√5/17). The line CE goes from C=(8,0) to E; let a parametric point be C+t(E-C). Its x-coordinate is 8-120t/17; setting x=2 gives t=17/20, hence the y-coordinate of P is (17/20)(24√5/17)=6√5/5. For BD, because BD is the angle bisector of angle B, D is on AC and AD:DC=AB:BC=7:8, so D=(8A+7C)/15=(24/5,8√5/5). The line BD goes from B=(0,0) to D; let a parametric point be sD. Its x-coordinate is 24s/5; setting x=2 gives s=5/12, hence the y-coordinate of Q is (5/12)(8√5/5)=2√5/3. P and Q are both on the vertical line AH, so PQ equals the difference of the y-coordinates: PQ=6√5/5-2√5/3=(18-10)√5/15=8√5/15.
